full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts, for the disposal of this appeal, are that the respondents filed the aforesaid suit seeking declaration of their title to 1.84 acres of land. (They added the prayer for partition in the revisional stage) stating, inter alia, that the land appertaining to R.S. Khatin No. 21 measuring an area of 12.95 acres along with other lands originally belonged to Rajmohon, Ketu and Panchu, Rajmohon got 4.27 acres of land in his share and after his death, his 8 sons Kailash, Rasik, Rojoni, Surjokanto, Rakhal, Piyari and Choto incherited his share. Ketu, while residing with his brother Rajmohon, executed a Will on 17.02.1913 in favour of his nephew Kailash to the extent of 12 annas and to his wife Feli to the extent of 4 annas share specifically pointing out that on her demise Kailash would get his entire share. Accordingly, after the death of Feli, Kailash got Ketu's share to the extent of 4.27 acres of land by virtue of the said Will. He also inherited a share as son of Rajmohan. Jogesh Chandra, being only son of Kailash, inherited the entire share left by Kailash but in the R.S. Khatian only 4 annas share was recorded in his name though he acquired 6 annas share out of the total land. Panchu died leaving two sons, Kanai Lal and Kalicharan @ Khoka but in the R.S. and S.A. Khatians more shares were recorded in their names. Jogesh Chandra transferred 1.34 acres of land out of his 4.86 acres, by registered kabala dated 19th August 1957, in favour of the plaintiff No. 1, his mother Maloti and the plaintiff No. 4. On the same day, Jogesh, by another deed, transferred 1.34 acres of land in favour of Kishore, Mohananda and Satish, the predecessor's of the plaintiffs. Kalicharan @ Khoka, by a registered dated 2nd June 1958 exchanged .84 acre of land with Mohananda, Kishore and Satish. Pursuant to that exchange deed, Kishore, Mohananda and Satish got lands of Shakhari Kati Mouja and Kalicharan got lands of the Gaokhali Mouja. Mohananda died leaving on issue and, accordingly, Kishore inherited his share and on the death of Kishore, the plaintiffs got his share. Satish, died without any issue and, accordingly, the plaintiffs got his share. Thus, the plaintiffs are entitled to get decree to the extent of 1.84 acres of land. 

 3. The defendant Nos.1-3 contested the suit by filing written statement contending that in the suit khatian Rajmohon, Ketu and Panchu had 13.13 acres of land and, accordingly, each brother got 4.38 acres. Rajmohon died leaving behind 8 sons and each son inherited .49½ acre of land. Ketu died leaving without any issue and, therefore, his brother Panchu inherited his share. Thus, Panchu got 8.75 acres of land. Out of 13.13 acres of land, Rajmohon, Panchu and Ketu settled 1.16 acres to different tenants. Panchu, in fact, got 7.86 acres of land after the settlement. After his death, Kanai and Kalicharan, his two sons, inherited the same. Kanai died leaving 4 sons Judhusthir, Nittynnanda, Gouranga and Narayan, who transferred 3.93 acres of land in favour of defendant No.3 by executing 5 sale deeds. The sale deeds and deed of exchange as mentioned in the plaint by the plaintiffs were forged and collusive and they did not acquire any title to the said lands on the basis of those deeds. 

 9. It was the case of the plaintiffs that the land measuring an area of 12.83 acres of R.S.Khatian No.21 originally belonged to Rajmohan, Ketu and Panchu. Each brother got 4.27 acres of land in their respective shares. Rajmohan died leaving 8 sons Kailash, Rashik, Rojoni, Surjokanto, Rakhal, Piyari and Choto. It was the further case of the plaintiffs that Ketu, having had no issue, executed a Will on 17.02.1913 in favour of Kailash to the extent of 12 annas and to his wife Feli to the extent of 4 annas share out of his share. There was a stipulation in the said Will that after the death of Feli, her interest would be devolved upon Kailash by virtue of the Will. Accordingly, after the death of Feli, Kailash got entire 'Ard share of Ketu, that is, to the extent of 4.27 acres of land. It was the claim of the plaintiffs that Kailash, by virtue of the Will and as son of Rajmohon, acquired 4.86 acres of land. Thereafter, Kailash died leaving only son Jogesh Chandra as his heir. Panchu died leaving behind two sons Kanai and Kalicharan. Jogesh sold 1.34 acres to the plaintiffs on 19.08.1957. He again sold 1.34 acres of land to Kishore, Mohananda and Satish, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs by another deed dated 19.08.1957. Kalicharan exchanged his .84 acre of land with Kishore, Mohananda and Satish by a deed of exchange dated 02.06.1958. Mohananda died without issue and his share was devolved to Kishore. Satish died leaving plaintiffs No.1-3 as his heirs. 

 16. The plaintiffs in their plaint initially stated that the land measuring an area of 12.95 acres appertaining to R.S. Khatian No.21 and Plots Nos.2208, 2209, 2210, 2211, 2212, 2213, 2214, 2215, 2216, 2219, 2221 and 2280 of Gowkhali Mouza belonged to Kailash, Harihor, Kiron Chanda, Rajanikanta, Kartick, Brata Beway, Fulmala, Koti Sundari, Kanai Lal and Kalicharan in their respective shares in different groups. It was their further case that those lands were recorded in S.A. Khatian Nos.39,213,217,311 and 194. From S.A. Khatians ext.3 series it appears that the land measuring an area of 7.96 acres of plots Nos.2209, 2210, 2211, 2212 and 2213 appertaining to S.A. Khatian No.39 was recorded in the names of Kanai Lal and Kali Charan. The land measuring an area of .70 acre of Plot No.2208 of S.A. Khatian No.213(Ext. 3 Ka) was recorded in the name of Jogesh Chandra son of Kailash Chandra Halder. The land measuring .92 acre of plots No.2215 and 2280 appertaining to S.A. Khatian No.217 (Ext.3Kha) was recorded in the name of Rajani Kanta. The land measuring 1.74 acres of Plot Nos.2214, 2215, 2221, 2280 and 2220 appertaining to S.A. Khatian No.31 1(ext. 3Ga) was recorded in the names of Harihor and Keron Chandra and the land measuring an area of .95 of Plots No.2215, 2216 and 2219 appertaining to S.A. Khatian No. 154 (ext.3 gha) was recorded in the name of Brata Bewa. From Ext.1 (R.S. Khatian No.21) it appears that name of Kailash, father of Jogesh, was recorded to the extent of 4' annas share but in remarks column, which is the column regarding the name of the possessor, his name was mentioned against plot No.2208 in respect of .70 acre of land only which was subsequently recorded in S.A. Khatian No. 213(ext.3Ka) in S.A. operation. In his cross examination P.W.1 has said "এস,এ, খতিয়ানে যোগেশের ৭০ শতক রেকর্ড হওয়া দৃষ্ট হয়।" Jogesh did not take any step to get the S.A. khatian corrected claiming more land by virtue of the disputed Will. 

 17. By way of amendment of the pleading, the plaintiffs added that the land measuring an area of 12.83 acres appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.311 and Plots No.5794, 5495, 5496, 5497, 5498, 5501, 5502, 5503, 5504, 5505 and 5506 belonged Rajmohan, Katu and Panehu. Rajmohon having 4.27 acres of land died leaving 8 sons Kailash, Rashik, Rajani, Kartic, Surjakanta, Rakhal, Peari and Chuta. Katu, having had no issue, executed a Will in favour of brother's son Kailash and wife Fell on 17.02.1913 in respect of 12 annas and 4 annas shares respectively. That is, the said will was executed before C.S. operation. P.W.1 in his cross-examination has said, “আমার বয়স ৫০/৫২। ১৭-০২-১৯৩ ইং তারিখের দলিল সম্পর্কে আমার ব্যক্তিগত ধারনা নাই।” He further said, "সি, এস এ কেতুরামের নামে রেকর্ড আছে " From the pleadings, evidence mentioned above, C.S. khatian (ext. Ka), R.S. Khatian (ext.1) and S.A. Khatians (ext 3 series) it appear that those records were not prepared in accordance with the terms of alleged Will (Ext 7). It is to be mentioned here that in the schedule of Will (ext.7) names and particulars of the properties Willed were not mentioned. Though Will was allegedly executed on 17.02.1913 and C.S. Khatian was prepared and published thereafter, the same was not prepared in accordance with the terms of alleged Will rather the same was prepared and published in the names of Ketu (the alleged testator) and his two brothers Rajmohan and Panchu. C.S. Khatian has got presumptive value though rebutable. An entry in C.S. record-of-right is presumed to be correct until the contrary is shown. The C.S. record-of-right being prepared with considerable formality and the proceedings of Revenue Officers being conducted with publicity, the entries in such records should not be lightly discarded. From the preparation of C.S. Khatian in the name of Ketu, two things are clear which are (1) at the time preparation of Khatian Ketu was alive and (2) the same was not prepared in accordance with the terms of alleged Will. The plaintiffs did not take any step to rebut the presumption of C.S. Khatian. It appears from the transfer deed dated 29.8.1957 executed by Jogesh son of Kailash in favour of Kammakkhya and others (ext.4) and deed dated 29.8.1957 executed by said Jogesh to Kaishore Halder and others (ext.5) he did not recite that he had acquired title to the land transferred by virtue of the Will executed by Ketu to his father Kailash. After 85 years of alleged execution of Will the plaintiffs, for the first time, disclosed about the existence of the Will. The last Court of facts rightly drew conclusion that the Will is a suspicious document. The suspicion of the Court of facts has got basis because- (1) the plaintiffs disclosed about the Will after 85 years of its execution; (2) No evidence has been adduced in respect of its execution, attestation and recitation to the testator; (3) No date of death of the testator has been mentioned in the pleadings or in evidence to decide the issue whether probate of the Will was mandatory or not; (4) C.S., R.S. and S.A. khatians were not prepared fol-lowing the terms of the Will; (5) In the recital of sale deeds of '1957 there were no recitation that Jogesh acquired title to 4.86 acres of land from his father Kailash, who got the same on the basis of Will and (6) Neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessor paid any rent of the suit land since last 85 years. 

 19. The High Court Division in its judgment has given much importance on the point that since will was executed before enforcement of the Succession Act, 1925 it was not required to be probated. It is the settled principle that the declaration made in the Will should be operative after the death of the testator and not before that. In this case, we do not find anything either in the plaint or in the evidence as to the date of death of the testator Ketu which was relevant for the decision whether probate of the instant Will was mandatory or not. We have already found from the admission of P.W.1 that C.S. Khatian was prepared in the name of Ketu (not in the name of Kailash) which indicates that Ketu was alive at the time of preparation of C.S. Khatian. So, it is difficult to say that at the time of enforcement of the Succession Act in 1925 Ketu was not alive. In the case of Hem Nolini Vs. Isolyne Sarojbashini reported in AIR 1962 SC 1471 subject matters were three Wills. One was of April 1921, second one was of June 1925 and third one was of April 1930. No probates of the first and second Will were taken out. Testator died in 1934. In such circumstances Supreme Court of India observed that no person can claim as a legatee or as an executor unless he obtains probate or letters of administration of the Will under which he claims. 

 21. Since C.S. and R.S. and S.A. Khatians were not prepared and published in accordance with the terms of the Will and the same came into light after 85 years of its execution and no evidence was led to prove the Will to satisfy the conscience of the Court that it was the last Will of a free and capable testator so, it is difficult to accept that the Will has been duly proved. Moreover, the last Court of facts, considering the evidence, held that the Will has not been acted upon. Since the requirements of law is that the Will should be attested by two or more witnesses, each of whom has seen the testator to sign and should sign the Will in the presence of the testator, the Court while examining the question as the Will propounded has been duly executed by the testator of the Will, whether the same suffers from suspicious circumstances and it is the last Will and testament of the testator, Will have to be care-fully analysed upon examining the evidence adduced before the Court. In this case, the revisional Court reversed the finding of facts arrived at by the last Court of facts ignoring the above requirements of law.
